Captured detailed technical requirements (Level2 only) ​

LU2-SK04 — Node.js Core: ability to build and execute small CLI or service scripts using core modules without heavy guidance ability to read and write files asynchronously using callbacks, promises, and fs APIs ability to manage process lifecycle, exit codes, standard input, standard output, standard error, and environment configuration knowledge of timers, buffers, streams, and events for common application tasks ability to install dependencies and use package.json scripts while distinguishing core modules from packages

LU2-SK05 — Node.js Development Tools: ability to configure common development tools for linting, formatting, and test execution in a Node.js codebase knowledge of how package scripts coordinate development workflows across build, test, and serve tasks ability to use debugger and logging tools to trace application behavior during local development ability to make routine changes to tool configuration files with occasional guidance from documentation

LU2-SK06 — Node.js Service Development: ability to design and implement CRUD services with validation, error handling, and structured logging knowledge of middleware, routing, and service-layer composition patterns ability to connect services to databases and external APIs with basic retry and timeout settings ability to write unit and integration tests for service behavior and use debugging tools

LU2-SK07 — Node.js Frameworks: ability to build simple CRUD endpoints or pages using framework conventions ability to apply middleware for authentication, validation, and basic error handling ability to manage configuration, environment variables, and package dependencies in a working application ability to troubleshoot common setup and runtime issues with documentation support

LU2-SK08 — Node.js Performance Optimization: ability to identify core performance concepts such as CPU usage, memory consumption, event loop activity, and I O latency knowledge of basic profiling and benchmarking approaches used to review Node.js application behavior ability to recognize synchronous code paths that can delay request handling and reduce responsiveness knowledge of simple caching and connection reuse practices that reduce repeated work

LU2-SK09 — Node.js Security: knowledge of Node.js security fundamentals, including authentication, authorization, and input validation ability to recognize common insecure coding patterns such as hardcoded secrets, weak password handling, and unsanitized input knowledge of common web application threats relevant to Node.js, including cross site scripting and injection attacks ability to follow documented secure configuration guidance for environment variables, package settings, and runtime options

LU2-SK10 — Web Communication Protocols: ability to construct and inspect basic HTTP requests and responses using standard headers and payloads knowledge of how cookies, sessions, and authentication tokens support stateful web interactions ability to explain the difference between synchronous request-response flows and asynchronous browser communication knowledge of common transport and security concepts such as TLS, certificate validation, and encrypted traffic ability to use documentation and basic tooling to troubleshoot simple communication issues

LU2-SK11 — Cloud Fundamentals: Cloud Compute Services: Familiarity with VMs, containers, and concepts like scalability in cloud compute services. Serverless Computing: Knowledge of serverless concepts, ability to develop and deploy serverless functions or applications. Cloud Storage Services: Some practical experience of object storage, block storage, or some file storage. Cloud Database Services: Practical experience of some Cloud databases (relational, NoSQL). Cloud Integration and Messaging Services: Basic understanding and some practical experience of some async ways of service communication, queues, message brokers Understanding of Cloud Service Models: IaaS, PaaS, SaaS and FaaS. Practical experience of usage. Basic understanding of cloud security best practices. Good understanding of at least one cloud provider's offerings within one or more cloud technology domains (i.e., Serverless, Containers, Edge Computing, Internet of Things (IoT), etc.).

LU2-SK12 — Node.js Infrastructure and Clouds: ability to describe common infrastructure components used by Node.js applications, including compute, storage, networking, and runtime dependencies knowledge of basic cloud service models and typical deployment targets such as virtual machines, containers, and managed platforms ability to follow documented steps to configure environment variables, secrets, and application settings for a single environment knowledge of foundational concepts for logging, health checks, and basic process management in a cloud host

LU2-SK13 — Node.js Database Experience: ability to run parameterized queries and basic ORM or query builder operations ability to manage connection pooling and handle routine database errors in application code knowledge of transaction usage for multi step data changes ability to retrieve and persist application data within a working Node.js service

LU2-SK14 — Software Engineering Knowledge & Experience: Knowledge of implementation details for different Data Structures, Networks principles encryption/decryption using Symmetric-Key Algorithm and public key encryption systems Ability to create complex queries and sql-scripts (several tables, create/delete/drop, select with join etc., merge tables) ability to create and configure virtual machines, snapshots, backup, virtual devices, deployment containers using some virtualization tools Ability to troubleshoot complex issues like multithreading,etc. Ability to use most IDE features. Knowledge of main Software Licenses.

LU2-SK15 — Common security knowledge: Basic attack vectors awareness (like XSS, SSRF, CSRF, injections). Basic understanding of application security mechanisms including security controls and countermeasures.

LU2-SK16 — Docker: Know how image tags, digests, and registry authentication affect image retrieval and identification. Explain how published ports, container DNS, and user-defined networks support communication between containers. Can configure an existing Docker Compose application with environment variables, health checks, and service dependencies. Have experience improving a basic Dockerfile by applying build caching and running the application as a non-root user. Proven experience troubleshooting common startup, networking, and file-permission failures using logs, inspect data, and container shells. Have experience integrating an existing Docker build into a CI/CD pipeline that runs tests and pushes an image to a registry.

Personal evidence and progression ​

Use the ladder checkpoints as the learner scorecard. For each checkpoint, change not assessed → practising → demonstrated → needs refresh, recording an evidence path/date and limitations. To demonstrate a checkpoint: explain the mechanism without notes, implement a representative task independently, diagnose an injected failure, and justify the trade-offs. A level remains unassessed until every checkpoint at that level and prerequisite levels has evidence; do not infer your ability from how many notes were written.
